clue.text: Bloomer made by priest after broadcast in US city

indicators.note: in places the broadcast-and-priest pair inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: after puts the priest following the broadcast in the order of letters

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by a clergyman after going on air in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobelia is a flowering garden plant, and anything that flowers can be called a bloomer.

clue.text: Foil a natural process

definitions.meaning: foil is metal beaten into a thin sheet, also called this word (gold ___)
in biology a process is an outgrowth from a body, and a plant's green blade is such an outgrowth

explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet is called gold or silver leaf, and a plant leaf is a natural outgrowth, a process in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Its great size limits hostilities

indicators.note: limits means bounds on each side, so the size word surrounds the hostilities word

parts.note: bulk means great size
hostilities means war

explanation.surface: Something so big that it keeps fighting in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a description of a defensive wall, whose bulk holds back war.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulwark is a massive defensive rampart, whose sheer mass keeps attackers out.

clue.text: I turn up in class, going over Aristotelian theories

indicators.note: going over means travelling back across, so the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction
up in means lodged inside, so the first person and the turn sit within the class abbreviation

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a philosophy class to review Aristotle's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' looks like 'arrive', but 'turn' is a go and 'going over' is the reversal; 'up in' puts I GO inside CL, making CIGOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle founded formal deductive reasoning, so his theories of argument are the classic system of reasoning.

clue.text: Porter, possibly, follows fine, richly-coloured dog

indicators.note: follows puts the beer after the fine-and-coloured letters

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in letters
red is a rich colour
porter is a dark beer, an example of ale

explanation.surface: A railway porter trails behind a handsome, ruddy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a station porter but is the dark beer; A1 (first-class) is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Increase number of soldiers relieving us in a month

indicators.note: relieving means taking over from, as one sentry relieves another, so the soldiers replace the us letters

parts.note: August is a month
men means a number of soldiers

explanation.surface: Bolster troop numbers by sending some to take over from us during one month.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the US in AUGUST for MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to enlarge or add to it.

clue.text: The stress may be acute

parts.note: reads like severe tension, but stress here is emphasis on a syllable, and acute is a mark written over a vowel

explanation.definitionFit: An emphasis on a syllable is called this, and an acute is one kind of written mark over a letter.

clue.text: Aid to boarding crew has put down roughly

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers
to plank something down is to set it down heavily, a variant of plonk

explanation.surface: A ship's crew roughly laid down a boarding aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. To 'plank' (or plonk) something down is to set it down clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the movable walkway used to step on board a ship.

clue.text: Listener's part in getting noble man honoured?

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour, so an honoured person has one

explanation.surface: Where a nobleman gets decorated, asks the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listener' is someone who hears, so the listener's part is a piece of the ear. OBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy bottom of the ear is part of what a hearer hears with.

clue.text: In Paris I settled in aircraft with unknown flight path

indicators.note: settled in means lodged inside, so the French pronoun sits within the aircraft word

parts.note: a tractor is an aircraft with its propeller at the front, pulling it along
je is French for I
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A French speaker settles into a plane with an unknown route.
explanation.walkthrough: A tractor here is not a farm vehicle but a plane with a front-mounted, pulling propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: The trajectory is the curve a projectile or flying body follows.

clue.text: 3 real twists relating to symbolism

indicators.note: twists signals a reworking of the letters into another order

parts.note: the answer to clue 3 (3-down) is the word for reasoning

explanation.surface: Genuine turns of argument concern symbolic meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' stands for the answer to 3-down, LOGIC; mix it with REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story in which characters and events stand for hidden meanings, a form of symbolism.

clue.text: Woman not quite conforming to convention

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: normal means conforming to the usual standard

explanation.surface: A lady who is a little unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's first name, a classic crossword way to clue a name.

clue.text: Subject to mishap, lying face downwards by chance

indicators.note: by means beside, so the chance word sits next to the lying word

parts.note: an accident is a chance event
prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: Someone liable to mishaps happens to be lying flat on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by chance' reads as one phrase meaning accidentally, but 'by' places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is accident-prone is likely to suffer mishaps.

clue.text: Family line standing out as domestically fussy

parts.note: a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor
proud means projecting above a surface

explanation.surface: A dynasty that stands out for its home-loving fastidiousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. 'proud' in carpentry means sticking up above the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A house-proud person takes great, often excessive, care over the tidiness of their home.

clue.text: What gall, restoring the monarchy on this day!

definitions.text: What gall, restoring the monarchy on this day!

parts.words: What gall, restoring the monarchy on this day!
parts.note: gall here is a growth on a tree, not cheek; and 29 May, a holiday marking Charles II's restoration in 1660, was named after such a growth from an oak

explanation.definitionFit: The oak growth caused by wasps names Oak Apple Day, 29 May, when the 1660 Restoration of Charles II was celebrated.

clue.text: Sustain spectators, all initially getting stuck in to spread

indicators.note: getting stuck in means being inserted, so the first letter goes inside the pair of words

parts.note: to prop something is to sustain it
the gate is the number of spectators at a match

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word all

explanation.surface: Supporters at a game, every one of them getting stuck in, keep the cause spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. A gate is a crowd attendance at a British sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate something is to spread it widely, as with ideas or plants.

clue.text: Special aptitude for identifying ancient currency

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight and money used in ancient Greece and the Middle East

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a gift or knack, and also an ancient weight of silver or gold used as money.

clue.text: Tartans should be so suitable for purchasing, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the phrase is spoken, so we want a word sounding the same

parts.note: saleable means fit to be sold and bought

explanation.surface: Scottish plaid fabrics ought to be marketable, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tartans' suggests plaid cloth, but a tartan (or tartane) is also a small single-masted Mediterranean ship, which ought to be seaworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartan is a small Mediterranean vessel, and any ship should be fit to navigate on water.

clue.text: Bully loses head, chasing son in battle zone

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the trimmed bully comes after the son
loses head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to hector is to bully

explanation.surface: A bully, decapitated, pursues a boy into the war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a designated area of military operations.

clue.text: Is supporter on course able to name eating-place?

parts.note: can means is able to
a tee is the peg holding up a golf ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: A question about whether a golf caddie can recommend a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Is supporter ... able to' as the question 'CAN TEE?', so 'Is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria at a workplace or school.

clue.text: Cat's showing pleasure, mostly stalking birds — it grows

indicators.note: stalking means following behind, so the cat's sound comes after the birds

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a cat's purr shows contentment

explanation.surface: A happy cat purrs while hunting birds, and a plant grows nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it grows' is a deliberately vague definition for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, a plant, which is a living thing that grows.

clue.text: Choose to dispense with long-handled tool

parts.note: pick means choose
to axe something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: Decide to do without a long-handled implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickaxe is a digging tool with a pointed iron head on a long wooden shaft.

clue.text: It may nominally link a couple of barrels

definitions.text: It may nominally link a couple of barrels

parts.words: It may nominally link a couple of barrels
parts.note: barrels suggests casks or guns, but here means the parts of a double-barrelled surname, joined by a short dash

explanation.definitionFit: Double-barrelled British surnames such as Bowes-Lyon join their two parts with this punctuation mark.

clue.text: Quiet colleague's about to enter cabinet, upset regarding form of words

parts.note: p (piano) means quiet in music

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so the jumbled colleague sits within the jumbled cabinet
upset means knocked over, so the letters of cabinet are rearranged
about means moved around, so the colleague's word is jumbled

parts.note: an ally is a colleague, so ally's is the possessive

explanation.surface: A quiet associate is set to join the cabinet, causing a stir about wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' jumbles ALLYS into SYLLA, and 'upset' turns CABINET into ENTABIC; SYLLA goes inside after ENTA. Pentasyllabic means having five syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-syllabled describes words made of five units of sound, a feature of verbal form.

clue.text: Quickly formed opinion about soldiers, identifying headgear

indicators.note: about means around, so the opinion word encloses the soldiers

parts.note: a bet is an opinion, as in 'my bet is'
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A snap judgement about troops, based on what they wear on their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identifying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a soft round flat cap, worn by soldiers among others.

clue.text: Run fast and fall heavily

definitions.meaning: to come down hard, as rain does in a downpour

explanation.definitionFit: To pelt is to rush along at full speed, and rain that pelts down falls hard.

clue.text: Work a long time producing 10, for example

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: Working for ages to produce a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link; '10' refers to 10-across, NORMA, Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a stage work by Bellini, an example of this sung dramatic form.

clue.text: Most bears in the wild remain inactive for months

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
most means all but one, dropping the last letter of the word bears

explanation.surface: Most wild bears sleep through the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wild' looks like a phrase, but 'wild' alone is the anagram signal: BEAR (most of BEARS) plus IN and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernating animals pass the winter in a dormant state.

clue.text: Debt-collector finally threatening long period in cell

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of debts

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word threatening

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: A menacing bailiff threatens a long stretch in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison cell.

clue.text: Short course brought back, thanks to petition

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter of the course is dropped

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

indicators.note: brought back means the thanks word is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A brief part of a meal is returned, with gratitude, in answer to a request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly.
